title: Scan tests, fixtures, benchmarks, and reporting surfaces for missed shared-module adoption
scope: H31 scan across tests/**, benchmark harnesses and query metadata, docs/report generators under tools/docs/**, reporting surfaces under tools/reports/**, and test/runtime helper surfaces under tools/testing/** and tools/test_times/**. Repository fixture contents under benchmarks/repos/** are intentionally treated as fixture payload, not as adoption targets.

summary.overallAssessment: This surface already has a healthy amount of local helper reuse, especially under tests/helpers, and that should not be flattened away. The real adoption opportunities are in report-generator CLI scaffolding, repeated temp-root and testing-env setup patterns, and surface-parity harnesses that are now clearly shared enough to deserve one maintained helper rather than many bespoke copies.

highestPriorityHotspots.category: test helper consolidation versus healthy local harnesses
highestPriorityHotspots.whyItMatters: The test tree has many helpers already; the goal is to distinguish healthy harness reuse from duplicated ad hoc setup.
Report tools repeat createCli, read/write JSON, and runner boilerplate in several places, which increases drift in user-facing reporting commands.
Tests still mix resolveTestCachePath, prepareIsolatedTestCacheDir, raw mkdtemp, and ad hoc env mutation patterns. Selective consolidation improves reliability without over-abstracting test intent.

hotspotMatrix.name: Healthy test-local harnesses should stay shared within tests, not be pushed into src/shared
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Treat these helper families as healthy test-local shared surfaces. Expand them selectively rather than replacing them with product-code helpers.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These helpers encode test semantics, isolation, and fixture convenience. That belongs in tests, not in production shared modules.
testsToRequire: Keep helper contract tests when extending test-env, test-cache, API harness, or parity harness helpers

hotspotMatrix.name: Temp-root and env setup still repeat around existing test helpers
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Prefer the existing test-cache and test-env helpers over raw mkdtemp or hand-rolled process.env mutation when the test is not intentionally asserting raw environment behavior.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These helpers already solve most of the reliability and cleanup concerns. Reusing them improves determinism without obscuring the purpose of the test.
testsToRequire: existing helper contract tests whenever test-cache or test-env is extended

hotspotMatrix.name: Report generator CLI scaffolding repeats across tools/reports and tools/docs
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Keep command-specific aggregation and rendering local, but consolidate repeated CLI-parse, JSON-output, and report-write scaffolding onto small shared helper layers where the semantics are identical.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These scripts are structurally similar at the edges but different in their core report logic. The payoff is in reducing boilerplate, not in collapsing all reports into one engine.
testsToRequire: report-format and output-contract tests for each script family affected
CLI help and canonical workflow tests when user-facing report commands change

hotspotMatrix.name: Analysis/API parity harnesses are now a real shared test surface
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Continue centralizing shared parity harness behavior in the existing helpers rather than allowing each parity suite to keep growing bespoke setup logic.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: These suites are already demonstrating the right direction. The remaining work is extending the helpers, not creating new parallel harness styles.

hotspotMatrix.name: Bench harnesses should share low-level helpers selectively, not flatten workload semantics
hotspotMatrix.recommendedAction: Share low-level CLI, JSON, and config primitives where exact fit exists, but keep benchmark workload logic local unless duplication is explicitly proven.
hotspotMatrix.whyThisWayIsBest: Benchmark scripts often differ in workload semantics more than in low-level mechanics. Over-consolidation would reduce clarity and debuggability.

mappings.problemSurface: Temp-root and env setup in tests
Report CLI scaffolding and JSON/report-write boilerplate
Parity harness and API fixture setup

localExceptions.reasonToRemainLocal: These are healthy test-local shared surfaces and should not be hoisted into production shared modules.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainOutOfScope: Fixture repository contents are test payload, not adoption targets.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainSelective: Bench workload semantics should stay local; only low-level helper reuse should be increased.

localExceptions.reasonToRemainMostlyLocal: Its aggregation and rendering logic is domain specific even if boilerplate helpers can be shared.
This generator has issue-program-specific logic and should only share small boilerplate pieces, not its core ledger assembly.

recommendedFollowUps.why: If report/file/JSON boilerplate still feels too fragmented after H31 adoption, create the dedicated filesystem/JSON/report helper family.
The healthy tests/helpers and parity harness results here are direct input to the shared test-harness/helper issue.
This scan will produce a prioritized cleanup queue once the broader shared-module findings are reduced.
